newsitem.title: GERMANY: German FDP deputy wants Waigel to ditch gold plan.
newsitem.headline: German FDP deputy wants Waigel to ditch gold plan.

text.p: A member of parliament from Germany's liberal Free Democrats (FDP), Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition partners, has called for Finance Minister Theo Waigel to withdraw his plan to revalue gold and currency reserves.

Juergen Koppelin, an FDP budget policy expert, was quoted in Saturday's edition of the Bild daily as saying damage caused by ramming the plan through against the will of the German central bank, the Bundesbank, would be too great.
"The finance minister wanted to fool us into believing that there would be no problems with the Bundesbank over the revaluation of the gold and currency supplies," Koppelin said.
"Waigel should now give up his plan. The psychological damage would be too great."
One member of Kohl's own Christian Democratic Union (CDU) has already declared he will not vote for legislation to approve revaluation against the will of the Bundesbank.
